statements.t: We also have adopted a Bitcoin treasury strategy and intend to hold Bitcoin as a treasury reserve asset.

Our business is built upon a foundational belief that Bitcoin represents a superior long-term store of value and a viable alternative to traditional fiat-based reserve assets, and we believe that Bitcoin will play an increasingly important role as a reserve asset for individuals, corporations and governments worldwide.
As we continue to develop and expand our platforms, we expect innovation, technology development, and disciplined capital allocation to remain important components of our strategy.
We do not expect the Silvia ETFs to generate meaningful revenue in the near term.
We expect to recognize the related severance and share-based compensation expense in the fourth quarter of 2026.

In evaluating our liquidity position, we considered our anticipated operating cash needs, the timing and nature of potential obligations under the Convertible Notes, our current cash and cash equivalents balance, and the availability of financing and capital-raising alternatives.

In the near term, we expect to use available resources primarily to fund operating expenses, working capital requirements, investments in technology and infrastructure, and the development of our asset management and exchange-traded fund businesses, including registration and compliance costs, personnel and systems, the General Partner’s capital contributions to the Initial Fund and seed capital, expense…
We expect these costs to increase in future periods and to be incurred before, and substantially in advance of, any related revenue.

In addition, we expect to pay aggregate severance of $1.5 million to our former Chief Financial Officer, Chief Operating Officer and Chief Legal Officer in equal monthly installments over the six months following their separations in October 2026.

Based on our assessment of our anticipated operating cash needs, potential obligations under the Convertible Notes, financial position, and available financing and capital-raising alternatives, we believe that the Company has sufficient resources to satisfy anticipated working capital and operating requirements for at least the next twelve months.

In addition, we intend to rely on the other exemptions and reduced reporting requirements provided by the JOBS Act.
